summary_rationale: Cheniere operates a premier 56 mtpa U.S. LNG export platform anchored by $112.2 billion of unsatisfied long-term transaction price (9-year weighted-average recognition) and strong project execution, having completed CCL Stage 3 ahead of guaranteed schedule and within budget in August 2026 while advancing Midscale Trains 8 & 9 (58.6% complete) and SPL Expansion Phase 1 (May 2026 Bechtel EPC, Sept 2026 Final EIS). However, Pass 1 blind-spot forensics confirm a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL profile with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health: (1) 9M 2026 volume growth leaned heavily on short-term marketing (352 TBtu, +73.4% YoY; 73% variable revenue share) during a Strait of Hormuz-driven TTF/JKM price surge (~$28.5/MMBtu in Oct 2026) that management warns may not recur as Venture Global (Plaquemines + CP2 29 mtpa), Golden Pass LNG and Qatari supply expand (EIA forecasts U.S. LNG exports rising +25.8% from 15.1 to 19.0 Bcf/d across 2025–2027); (2) gross consolidated debt expanded to $24.138 billion at Sept 30, 2026 (with a -$523 million working-capital deficit, 60.2% of net debt ring-fenced in 48.6%-owned CQP, 1.25x DSCR subsidiary covenants, declining capitalized interest, and an additional $1.2 billion 5.800% parent notes offering closed Nov 17, 2026 alongside $1.818 billion of 9M buybacks under a $10 billion 2026–2030 authorization); (3) June 2026 NPNS designation froze $349 million net IPM fair value into non-linear future COGS amortization while leaving 27% upstream IPM volumes on Level 3 MTM; (4) Q3 2026 customer concentration rose (Customers B and C at 14% and 11% of quarterly revenue; Customer A at 13% of receivables/contract assets); and (5) governance consolidated as CFO Zach Davis was promoted to President & CFO on Nov 12/16, 2026 while USTR Section 301 U.S.-built vessel mandates (1% in 2029 rising to 15% in 2047) loom over long-term logistics.
